sections.text: Chemical
Technical Procedure
Procedure
Introduction

This method covers the determination of nitrite 
 ion in water by using volumetric method.

The first draft was initiated by chemist : Amal 
 El-Gayar; reviewed by department director chemist: Zakia Soltan; revised by 
 quality control chemist: Mohamed Mosbah Mokpel and accepted by Eng. Awad M. Fatthy; Head Sector of Talkha Power Station
Significance

This method covers the 
titrimetric determination of nitrite in water and is applicable to waters 
containing nitrite ion in concentrations from about 3600 mg/L (ppm). Higher 
concentration may be determined by employing more concentrated potassium 
permanganate and sodium oxalate solutions.

The method is applicable where a complete freedom from interferences isn't 
required and is particularly applicable in systems containing a nitrite content 
greater than 5 ppm.
Summary of Method

A measured volume of sample is added below the 
surface of unknown volume of acidified potassium permanganate KMnO4.Under these conditions 
nitrite ions react only with permanganate ions. The 
solution is heated to complete the reaction. Excess permanganate is determined 
by adding a measured amount of sodium oxalate (excess), followed by back 
titration with standard permanganate solution.
Interferences

Reducing agents interfere with this method since 
it is essentially a means of measuring the reducing tendency. This does not 
detract from the utility of the method in many cases; for example, when 
nitrite is added to industrial water as a corrosion inhibitor and is present in 
relatively large quantities so that a small error is of little consequence. 
However, in those instances where relatively large quantities of other reducing 
agents are present the method is of lesser application.
Sampling

Nitrite ion should be determined as soon as possible after sampling, even when 
sterile bottles are used since bacteria naturally present in the 
water may cause conversion of all or part of nitrite to other materials 
such as nitrate or ammonia.

Keeping the sample cold, below 4.4oC 
( 40oF ), is helpful in minimizing nitrite 
conversion.
Safety Precautions

Collect the sample in 
sterile bottles.

The reagent used must 
be of sufficiently high purity to permit its use without lessening the 
accuracy of determination.

Water used for this 
method shall be free of nitrite ion and preferably sterile. This sterile water 
can be prepared by heating in an autoclave.

Nitrite-free water 
can be obtained by distillation, but preferably by the demineralization of 
distilled water, taking care to prevent absorption of nitrous fumes in the 
prepared water.

The pipette must be 
yield the required volume in one filling.

sections.text: Tools and Equipment
Apparatus

Pipettes 
Since, this method depends on the amount of 
KMnO4 consumed, it is imperative that pipetts for delivering the 
potassium permanganate standard solution and the sodium oxalate standard 
solution be calibrated and cleaned for maximum precision.
Reagents

Potassium Permanganate Standard Solution (0.04 
N).

Dissolve 2.5 gm of potassium permanganate in 2 
liters of boiling water in a Florence flask.
Cover with a beaker and simmer for h.
Cool to room temperature.
Filter twice by gravity through a fritted-glass filter and store in a dark-coloredstoppered glass bottle.

Pipette triplicate 50 ml aliquots of the Na2C2O4 
solution (0.04 N) into a 500-ml Erlenmeyer flask and add 100 ml of water

Heat to 90C 
and add 10 ml of sulfuric acid H2SO4 (1+1).

Titrate rapidly with potassium permanganate to a 
slight pink end point, persistent for 1 min.

Calculate the normality 
of the KMnO4 
solution. If necessary, adjust the normality to 
slightly less than the normality of the Na2C2O4 
solution and restandardize.

sections.text:
Sodium Oxalate Standard 
Solution (0.04 N)

Dry national bureau (Na2C2O4)
oxidimetric grade sodium oxalate, or equivalent, at 105C 
for 1h. and cool in a desiccator. Weigh 5.360 g, dissolve in water, and dilute 
to 2.0 liters. Store in a chemical resistant borosilicate glass container. 
Sodium oxalate solutions are subject to deterioration by microorganisms and 
should be prepared at time of use.

Sulfuric acid (1 + 1) 
 Carefully mix 1 volume of conc. 
H2SO4 ( Sp.Gr.1.84 ) into 1 volume of water.
Work to be Carried out

Add 50 ml of KMnO4 solution and 10 ml of 
H2SO4 (1+1 ) for each 50 ml sample up to a max. of 30 
ml of acid to a 500 ml Erlenmeyer flask.

Pipette a volume of sample 
containing 0.6 to 30.0 mg of nitrite ion to the flask by immersing the tip of the 
pipette below the surface of the KMnO4 solution.
A suitable sample volume is shown in Table 1.

Warm the solution in the 
flask to 90C 
immediately, the color change from purple color to brownish.
Add 50 ml of Na2C2O4 solution and swirl until colorless.

Titrate with KMnO4 
solution to a faint pink end point.

Determine the blank at 
the time of analysis, by repeating the procedure at least twice, using water 
equal in volume to the sample.
